rows.extracted_value: The innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) around a 10 solar mass black hole is approximately 29,886 meters.
rows.answer_text:
It seems like I might have misunderstood your request earlier. To find the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) for a Schwarzschild black hole, we can use the formula \( r_{\text{isco}} = 6GM/c^2 \), where \( G \) is the gravitational constant and \( M \) is the mass of the black hole.

For a 10 solar mass black hole:
\[ r_{\text{isco}} = 6 \times (10 \times M_\odot) \times GM_\odot/c^2 \]
Since \( GM_\odot/c^2 \approx 1.477 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{solar radii} \), we get:
\[ r_{\text{isco}} = 6 \times (10) \times 1.477 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{solar radii} \]
\[ r_{\text{isco}} = 9.462 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{solar radii} \]

However, this is not in SI units. To convert to meters:
\[ r_{\text{isco}} = 6 \times (10) \times GM/c^2 \]
Given \( G = 6.67430 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{m}^3/\text{kg s}^2 \), and the mass of the Sun \( M_\odot = 1.989 \times 10^{30} \, \text{kg} \):
\[ r_{\text{isco}} = 6 \times (10) \times (6.67430 \times 10^{-11}) \times (1.989 \times 10^{30}) / (299792458)^2 \]
\[ r_{\text{isco}} = 6 \times 10 \times 1.477 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{solar radii} \times 695700 \, \text{meters per solar radius} \]
\[ r_{\text{isco}} = 30 \times 1.477 \times 10^{-5} \times 695700 \, \text{meters} \]
\[ r_{\text{isco}} = 29886 \, \text{meters} \]

So the innermost stable circular orbit around a 10 solar mass black hole is approximately **29,886 meters**.

Answer: The innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) around a 10 solar mass black hole is approximately 29,886 meters.
